title: link
description:
Client -> daemon. NOT bridge-intercepted: it is forwarded verbatim and consumed by the motion daemon (L2: network_broker -> net_wd.configure), which is why it lives in daemon/ despite riding the data channel. The network path the client resolved to, which SELECTS THE ROBOT'S WATCHDOG PROFILE (LAN 150/500 ms vs WAN 300/1000 ms).

This is a safety input, not a hint. Reporting "lan" over a WAN path gives you a dead-man window tighter than your latency can hold, and the robot will ramp to a stop mid-motion; reporting "wan" on a LAN path merely loses responsiveness, so "wan" is the safe default when unsure.

Derive it from the SELECTED ICE candidate pair: both candidates host => "lan", anything else (srflx via STUN, relay via TURN) => "wan". Prefer the pair the transport reports as selected, and fall back to a nominated pair only when it is also in state "succeeded" -- a nominated-but-failed pair can otherwise claim "lan" on a relayed link.

Send it on control-channel open and again whenever the path changes; the ordering of channel-open and path-resolution is not guaranteed, so sending twice is expected.
